paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The writer sells the put, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. In a margin account the same short put is collateralised differently: the broker holds only a **margin requirement**, a fraction of the purchase price computed under exchange and FINRA minimum rules, and the writer keeps the rest of their buying power free for other positions [S6]. If the put is assigned, the writer is obliged to take the shares at the strike [S2]. **LEAPS** are listed options with more than a year until expiration, and they trade and settle exactly like shorter options [S3]. A **poor man's covered call** is a long, deep in-the-money LEAPS call paired with a short, near-term, out-of-the-money call on the same stock [S5].

The regime was labelled {{regime.label}} with a VIX of {{regime.vix}} and a risk-free rate of {{regime.risk_free_rate_pct|pct}}. The sizer put {{allocation.csp_pct|pct}} of the strategy budget into cash-secured puts, {{allocation.leaps_pct|pct}} into LEAPS, and left {{allocation.cash_pct|pct}} in cash, with a tilt of {{allocation.tilt}}.

The good-to-own screen is a quality gate applied before any trade is sized: it checks that a stock is on the curated list and has not fallen too far below its recent high, so that the writer is not taking assignment of a deteriorating business. The universe of trending tickers is filtered through this list, and any ticker not on it is skipped rather than traded.

{{counts.quality_passed}} underlyings passed the quality screen and {{counts.quality_excluded}} were excluded: {{quality_screen.passed_tickers|list}}. The reasons given were: AAPL "{{quality_screen.passed[0].why}}", COST "{{quality_screen.passed[1].why}}", MSFT "{{quality_screen.passed[2].why}}", SBUX "{{quality_screen.passed[3].why}}", and NKE "{{quality_screen.passed[4].why}}". The trend board ranked other names higher, but those were skipped because they are not on the good-to-own list; the trend board is a secondary signal only.

In the bottleneck board, the top-scoring layer was {{bottlenecks.layers[0].name}} at {{bottlenecks.layers[0].score}} with thesis state {{bottlenecks.layers[0].thesis_state}}, followed by {{bottlenecks.layers[1].name}} at {{bottlenecks.layers[1].score}} with thesis state {{bottlenecks.layers[1].thesis_state}}, and {{bottlenecks.layers[2].name}} at {{bottlenecks.layers[2].score}} with thesis state {{bottlenecks.layers[2].thesis_state}}. This board is a secondary signal: it re-orders quality-gated stocks and never adds one.
